**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination — request for reconsideration**
- Member: Jordan Jennings
- Member ID: W990598603
- Reference number: POC-3F7F71F65B-18736
- Date of denial notice: August 8, 2026
- Requested service: Bunion surgery (hallux valgus), CPT 28296
- Governing policy: **Aetna CPB 0629 – Bunionectomy**, https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0629.html (last review 12/11/2025)

---

I am appealing Aetna's denial of coverage for the bunion surgery (CPT 28296) that my surgeon, Dr. Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery, requested and has documented as medically necessary for me. The notice dated August 8, 2026 states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the procedure. I am asking Aetna to reconsider that decision, because the plan's own published criteria in Aetna CPB 0629 – Bunionectomy set out specific imaging measurements, and the weight-bearing X-ray already in my file meets them.

Below I have set out the plan's own language, exactly as it appears in that policy, next to what my records show.

### 1. The imaging criteria in the plan's policy

The policy states:

> "Radiographic confirmation Footnotes for Radiographic confirmation * of the most recent weight-bearing view X-ray demonstrating both of the following: An HVA of 30 degrees or greater; and An inter-metatarsal angle (IMA) (formed by the long axis of the first and second metatarsals) of 12 degrees or greater; and"

My records state that weight-bearing foot radiographs taken on June 23, 2026 showed a **hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees** and an **intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees**. Both numbers are above the thresholds the plan itself published. The imaging is a weight-bearing study, it is the most recent imaging in my chart, and it exceeds each measurement the policy names.

The policy also states:

> "Radiographic confirmation must include interpretation and report of weight bearing anterior/ posterior and lateral views of the affected foot."

If the concern is the form of the imaging record rather than the measurements, I would like to resolve it. My surgeon's office can send the full radiology interpretation and report for the June 23, 2026 weight-bearing study directly to Aetna on request. [Confirm with Dr. Reyes's office that the report for 2026-06-23 includes anterior/posterior and lateral views of the affected foot, and attach the report.]

Because the denial notice does not identify which specific imaging finding was considered insufficient, I am also asking Aetna to tell me, in writing, which criterion in CPB 0629 it applied and what in the imaging it found lacking.

### 2. Conservative treatment

The policy states:

> "The member's pain and symptoms over the medial bony eminence or calluses persist, making walking difficult despite at least a 6-month trial of conservative treatment under the direction of a healthcare professional that includes the following:"

and lists, among those measures:

> "Protective cushions/pads; Shoe inserts (generally contractually excluded); Corticosteroid injections; Debridement of hyperkeratotic lesions; Oral analgesics or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs);"

and:

> "Alternative or modified footwear that must include the following: Wearing well-fitting, low-heeled comfortable shoes made out of soft materials (e.g., canvas, cloth, soft leather) with wide toe box and padding; or"

> "Lace-ups or a combination last (front of the shoe is wider than the back of the shoe) that conforms to the bunion and minimizes irritation; and"

My records show:

- **14 months** of progressive foot pain that is not relieved by rest;
- **NSAIDs for 8 months**, with inadequate relief;
- a **corticosteroid injection on April 14, 2026**, which gave only about 4 weeks of partial relief;
- **wide toe-box footwear**, a **custom orthotic**, and activity modification, with 24 visits completed between March 21, 2026 and June 27, 2026, documented in the physical therapy discharge note;
- I **cannot tolerate closed shoes**, and my chart notes ulceration risk over the prominence.

That is conservative care under the direction of healthcare professionals spanning well beyond the six-month trial the plan describes, and my symptoms have persisted through all of it.

### 3. The additional findings the policy asks for

The policy states:

> "Documentation of skeletal maturity; and The member has one or more of the following:"

Among the conditions it then lists is:

> "Limited or painful range of motion at the first toe MTP joint; or"

My exam findings, as recorded, include positive provocative testing on the affected side and **range of motion limited by pain**. [Ask Dr. Reyes's office to confirm in a brief note whether the limited, painful range of motion is documented at the first MTP joint, and the date of that exam.] [Ask Dr. Reyes's office to supply documentation of skeletal maturity, which is not stated in the records I have.]

I want to be straightforward about one thing: several of the passages above end in a colon and introduce lists of further conditions that I have not seen reproduced in full. I am not going to characterize policy language I have not read. I am asking Aetna to identify the complete criteria it applied to my request so that my surgeon and I can respond to the right ones.

My records do not describe osteoarthritic changes on X-ray, and I am not claiming that finding. I am relying on the angle measurements, the documented course of conservative care, and the exam findings my surgeon recorded.

### What I am asking for

I ask Aetna to overturn the denial and authorize CPT 28296. In the alternative, I ask that the file be reviewed by a physician reviewer with relevant expertise and that I be told in writing which specific criterion of CPB 0629 my request did not satisfy, so that my surgeon can address it directly. Please also confirm receipt of this appeal.

I understand this appeal must be received by **February 4, 2027**. I am submitting it using Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form, available in my account at aetna.com under complaints, grievances and appeals, and sending it to **the appeal address printed on my denial letter** and/or by fax to **859-425-3379**. Aetna's member line is 1-800-872-3862 or the number on my card.

I am happy to provide anything further that would help. My surgeon's office has the complete chart and imaging and can release it on request.

Thank you for taking another look at this.

Sincerely,

_______________________________
